extracted.intended_audience: researchers applying for the Wellcome Discovery Award (grant applicants and their host organisations)
extracted.subtask_description: Filling in and justifying a full Discovery Award grant application to Wellcome, including research proposal, ethics, outputs management, animal and human participant details, costing and reviewer suggestions. The form gives required content, word limits and supporting documentation instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed start date
rubrics_metrics.description: The date must be at least seven months after the application deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can change your start date if your application is successful. All grant expenditure and activities must be within the grant start and end dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed length of funding (months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the requested length of funding in months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requesting support for greater than five years provide detailed workplan for first five years and outline only for remaining years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research subject area
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the most relevant area, based on the key aims of the research (e.g. Arts and Humanities; Brain and Behavioural Sciences; Cell Biology; Data Sciences; Genetics; Population and Public Health; Social Sciences etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information is used to report on our funding; select one area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research summary (maximum 200 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a summary of your proposed research, including key goals, for an expert audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We will use this as a short abstract and to classify your proposal; it may be published verbatim on our website so do not include confidential or commercially sensitive information. The summary should be as complete as possible within the word limit and include key words to enable text searching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of concurrent funding applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Is this or a similar application for funding currently under consideration elsewhere?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We will consider your application even if you have a similar application under review elsewhere. If another funder offers you funding you must tell us immediately and usually decide within one month. If you later apply elsewhere with a similar application, notify Wellcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Is this a resubmission of an application submitted to Wellcome?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 'Yes', explain how this application is different—significant changes are needed for the second application. You do not need to contact us first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research vision (maximum 3,000 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe your research vision showing how the research programme will be bold, creative and of high quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include aims and research questions, expected outcomes, background and prior work, approach and methods and how you will address challenges, key stages with locations and milestones. Ensure the research fits the Discovery remit. Do not include graphs/figures/tables in this description; use 'Additional information' for those. You may submit as text entry or PDF (11pt Arial, portrait).

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures and additional information (maximum two A4 pages, excluding Gantt charts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload any figures and additional information as a separate PDF; do not embed in the research vision description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more than two pages (excluding Gantt charts) the application will be returned to reduce information. Gantt charts illustrating project timeline are excluded from the two-page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: References (maximum 3,000 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include references needed to justify your proposal, with full citation including title and all authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In press publications may be included only if available on preprint servers. You can shorten references with more than 10 authors to 'et al' but ensure your position as author (if applicable) remains clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative AI disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you used generative AI in the writing of your application?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer 'No' if generative AI was only used for translation or to improve the standard of English. If 'Yes', provide brief details of how you used Generative AI and follow Wellcome's policy on Use of Generative AI in the Wellcome Application Process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human participants involvement screening
rubrics_metrics.description: Does your proposal involve human participants, human biological material (including cell lines) or data about living people?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wellcome uses WHO definition of research with human beings. Researchers using data that is not fully anonymised should answer 'Yes' and complete subsequent human-participant questions. Types of interventions and examples are listed. Read Wellcome's Research involving human participants policy for expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trial eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Does your proposal involve a clinical trial?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scheme supports trials that bring new understanding of social/biological processes and proof-of-concept studies; does not fund large clinical trials whose main purpose is to develop/test/implement a drug, product or intervention. Read Wellcome's clinical trials policy. If more than one clinical trial contact Wellcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design details for human participant research (maximum 800 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the study design, including number of participants per group, allocation method, type/frequency/duration of interventions, outcome measures, countries of research, sex/gender considerations, sample size justification and power calculations, methods to protect against bias, follow-up plans, long-term respondent care, and other significant risks to participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include proposed statistical analysis and explain methods to protect against bias (e.g. blinding, randomisation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment strategy and inclusion/exclusion criteria (maximum 300 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outline your recruitment strategy and describe inclusion/exclusion criteria for participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For clinical trials, describe how you will ensure inclusion of under-served groups as outlined in Wellcome's clinical trials policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient, participant and community involvement (maximum 200 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: How have you involved patients, participants, patient advocacy groups or communities in developing this proposal and what ongoing involvement will they have?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read Wellcome's advice on engaged research approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oversight arrangements (maximum 300 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the oversight arrangements for the study (e.g., Trial Steering Committee and Data and Safety Monitoring Board for clinical trials). If no separate oversight group, explain why not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For other study types (e.g., longitudinal/observational) describe membership and composition of any oversight group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and regulatory approvals (maximum 200 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Who has/will review the ethics of the project and when? Detail other regulatory approvals you have or will seek.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before research begins you must have ethical approval in every country where research will be carried out, relevant regulatory approvals for every site, and appropriate governance mechanisms. Any use of personal data or biological samples must comply with relevant legislation. Researchers outside the UK must describe local law/guidelines and how they will comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: NHS involvement and SoECAT requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Will you be using NHS facilities, staff or patients in the UK? If yes, have you completed a Schedule of Events Cost Attribution Tool (SoECAT) signed off by an AcoRD specialist?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By funding work needing NHS support, Wellcome abides by the Statement of Partnership on Non-commercial R&D in the NHS; you may not carry out research until NHS gives consent. You can submit SoECAT while application is reviewed but Wellcome cannot make a funding decision without it. Upload study info page and signed SoECAT summary if yes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal sponsor for project (maximum 100 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Which organisation(s) have agreed to act as formal sponsor for your project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All research involving human participants, tissue or data must have a sponsor who understands responsibilities and costs; typically a university or healthcare provider. Wellcome cannot act as sponsor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent for commercially exploitable results (maximum 200 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm you have or will try to get appropriate informed consent to use any potentially commercially exploitable results from data, tissues or samples derived from human participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no potentially commercially exploitable results will be produced, answer 'not applicable' and explain why. If addressed in outputs management plan you may refer to that answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental sustainability plan (maximum 300 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how you will undertake your proposed research in an environmentally sustainable way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include how you will reduce, reuse and recycle resources/equipment/materials; tools/initiatives to measure and reduce environmental impact; how you will minimise travel and emissions for grant participants and research participants. Also enter any total additional cost of undertaking the research sustainably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team composition and management (maximum 500 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the roles of all applicants and how the project will be managed and led.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requesting funds for staff working in different locations say where they will be working. Invite coapplicants through the application system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outputs management and sharing (Outputs Management Plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an outputs management plan that maximises health benefit by making research data, software and materials available with as few restrictions as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan should be clear, concise, proportionate and focus on how outputs will be identified, managed and used to advance health benefits. For each relevant output specify: what outputs will be generated; metadata/documentation accompanying outputs; when outputs will be made available; where outputs will be made available; how outputs will be discovered/accessed; any restrictions and justification; how data/metadata will be stored/backed up/preserved; resources dedicated to outputs management and ensuring FAIR (findable, accessible, interoperable, reproducible). Clinical trial-specific guidance applies where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property (IP) outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the IP your research will generate and how you will protect and use it to achieve health benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State any plans to allow collaborators or third parties to own/co-own/have exclusive access to Wellcome-funded IP and consider restrictions in grant condition 8. Provide contact details for your organisation's TTO or equivalent. Maximum 500 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach for maximising impact of outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Select an approach to maximise impact of significant research outputs: make outputs available for access and reuse; protect IP and/or commercialise; combination of both; or not applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the option that best matches your outputs management and IP plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborations: essential collaborators and IP assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Are any collaborations essential? List key collaborators and outline their role and resources contributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborators provide essential expertise/support/materials, are not normally involved in day-to-day running or intellectual design, are not remunerated (expenses may be covered). Collaborators must assign Wellcome-funded IP to lead applicant’s organisation in accordance with grant condition 8. Provide short description and confirm collaborators have agreed to be involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location of activity and fund attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Will funded activity take place at more than one location? For each location provide organisation, country and percentage of funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include administering organisation; enter approximate percentage of total funds spent in each location, enter zero for locations with activity but no significant funds. If requesting salary costs attribute them to employing organisation. Indicate if based at Wellcome Trust supported facilities and add them as a location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple direct award locations (conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Will you need funds to be awarded directly to more than one location? We will consider this only if: request includes multiple currencies with additional currencies at least equivalent to £750,000 OR involves an organisation based in a low- or middle-income country (LMIC) and Wellcome will assess financial capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If awarded directly to more than one location, Wellcome will not move funds between organisations after the award letter is issued. Explain why direct awards are needed and provide country, organisation and value/currency for each location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal research necessity and 3Rs (maximum 250 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why animal use is necessary and the choice of species; outline why no realistic non-animal alternatives exist and how approaches embed the principles of replacement, reduction and refinement (3Rs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify species choice especially when used as a model for a human condition. Consider replacement with tissues, reducing numbers, refining experimental design to maximise information from minimum animals. Refer to NC3Rs guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal species and total numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter the animal species and total numbers needed including animals purchased, bred or used to maintain colonies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include strain if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal sample size justification and statistical analyses (maximum 750 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide justification of proposed sample size, details of planned statistical analyses, inclusion of male and female sexes or justification for single-sex research, power calculations if appropriate, experimental design and methods to reduce bias such as blinding or randomisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure adequate experimental detail for each species to justify use and number of animals. Include unit of analysis, how sample/group size was derived, number of time points if repeated measures used, number of replications. Tables/figures may be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severity of procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate the severity classification of procedures (Sub-threshold, Mild, Moderate, Severe, Non-recovery).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 'Moderate', 'Severe' or 'Non-recovery' selected provide details of the procedures, whether lower severity procedures can be used, and when procedures were last reviewed by AWERB/IACUC (state year). Guidance on assessing severity available on Home Office website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home Office licences for UK procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Does your proposal include procedures to be carried out on animals in the UK which need a Home Office licence? If yes, is there a current Home Office Personal Project Licence (PPL) authorising the proposed procedures?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have a PPL provide the licence holder name; if not, detail plans and timelines for obtaining the appropriate licence. The organisation must ensure compliance with UK laws and regulations at all times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal work outside the UK: compliance and checklists
rubrics_metrics.description: If using animals or animal tissue outside the UK confirm the work will, at minimum, follow principles of UK legislation and comply with local legislation and ethical review procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For studies using non-human primates, cats, dogs or equines NC3Rs will review. For other species applicants should complete and upload NC3Rs checklists as appropriate. Upload checklists for rodents, rabbits, sheep, goats, pigs, cattle, Xenopus, zebrafish when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-human primates: additional detail
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-human primate research provide detailed answers on compliance with NC3Rs principles, transport needs and measures to minimise stress, housing and enrichment, single housing justification, experimental procedures and minimisation of pain/suffering, staff training and recent reviews by named oversight roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NC3Rs will review all applications involving primates or their tissue/data. Provide justification for any single housing, details on restraint/food/water restriction, training requirements and welfare reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cats, dogs and equidae: additional detail
rubrics_metrics.description: For research involving cats, dogs or equidae provide sourcing, transport minimisation measures, import arrangements, housing and environmental enrichment, socialisation/out-of-pen activity for dogs and pasture access for equines, single housing justification, procedures to minimise harm, monitoring and humane endpoints, and staff training requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NC3Rs will review all applications involving these species. Answer thoroughly even if using already generated tissue/data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genetically altered animals: welfare expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: All projects involving genetically altered mice are expected to consider welfare assessment principles set out by NC3Rs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow NC3Rs guidance on welfare assessment for genetically altered animals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual-use risk consideration (Risks of research misuse)
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm you have considered whether your proposed research could generate outcomes that could be misused for harmful purposes (dual use risks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of risky outcomes include demonstrating how to render vaccines ineffective, confer resistance to therapeutics, enhance virulence or transmissibility, evade diagnostics, enable weaponisation, or generate/reconstitute eradicated agents. Do not include remote/hypothetical risks, data reidentification/data breach risks, or safeguarding risks (these are managed separately). Refer to BBSRC/MRC/Wellcome policy and Good Research Practice guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and mitigation of tangible dual-use risks (maximum 250 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: If tangible dual-use risks are identified briefly describe them and explain how you and your organisation will manage them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk identification should balance benefits. Mitigation could include ongoing dual-use risk review, independent expert advice, monitoring during project, team awareness and education/training. Provide concrete steps to minimise risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom to operate and conflicts of interest (FTO/IP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any freedom to operate or other intellectual property related issues that might affect your ability to do the proposed research or to use, share or commercialise the outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If satisfied there are no issues answer 'not applicable' and explain briefly. Consider use of technology, software, databases, materials or patented inventions owned/controlled by others and whether you have written permission. Consider agreements that might restrict ownership/use/sharing with collaborators or third parties. Disclose all relevant information or refer to outputs management plan. See grant condition 8 and Wellcome IP guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Currency requested and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the currency you would like the grant to be paid in and state whether it is your local currency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If local currency not on the list you must cost in GBP, USD or EUR. Explain why you request costs in the selected currency and what exchange rate you used. If you don't have a bank account in the currency requested you will bear any conversion-related increases in research costs. See grant currency exchange policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff costs: detail and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Detail full employment costs for all staff to be funded on the grant, including role, number of staff, names if known (especially for posts handling non-human primates), salary grade/scale, basic annual starting salary, months on project, % time and cost requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide justification for the role and responsibilities, seniority and salary level. Costs must include employer contributions and statutory obligations. Costs for PhD/research masters fees for research assistants must be requested at application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant salary request and teaching buyout (evidence required)
rubrics_metrics.description: If requesting salary for lead/co-applicants or teaching buyout upload a letter from a senior member of each organisation confirming contract and institutional commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For salary requests the letter must confirm employment contract allows salary recovery and host organisation will underwrite the salary and post. For teaching buyout the applicant must retain at least 10% teaching time and buyout not provided by other grants. Combine letters as a single PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment support costs
rubrics_metrics.description: If you or a staff member employed on the grant is disabled or has a long-term health condition, you can request adjustment support costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter the cost of the adjustment support needed; no further information required at this stage. Wellcome offers support types to help do the project, report progress and attend events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and continuing professional development costs
rubrics_metrics.description: If requesting training and CPD, specify type (professional skills or research skills), description and cost requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide justification for training and CPD and describe the type of training requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials and consumables costs and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a high-level breakdown of materials and consumables costs (e.g., reagents, antibodies, cell culture, shipping, printing), with estimate per staff member per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the justification explain the estimate of cost for each staff member each year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animals budgeting and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: If requesting animals include species, total number to be bought, purchase cost, maintenance and procedures cost, and associated animal costs (training, enrichment, licences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure costing is done after consultation with animal house/biological services manager. Organisation must apply consistent costing methodology. Do not include justification of animal numbers here—use the 'Research involving animals' section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment costs, procurement and sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: If requesting equipment provide type, number of items, cost per item, maintenance contract cost and total cost requested. Consider cost-effectiveness and environmental sustainability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate should cover delivery, installation, maintenance and training. Expect manufacturer warranty for first year and Wellcome will fund reasonable maintenance costs for four years after warranty. For UK medical/veterinary equipment quote exclusive of VAT; for other equipment include VAT where applicable. Equipment costing £100,000 or more requires at least one formal quote including negotiated discounts. Provide justification for items >£100k (similar equipment available, why it cannot be used, other users).

rubrics_metrics.name: Access charges for shared equipment or facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Request costs for access to shared equipment/facilities essential to research, including materials/consumables plus proportion of maintenance/service contracts and staff time for dedicated technical staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not cover estates, utilities, depreciation or insurance or other staff not directly operating the facility. If facilities were paid for by Wellcome grant you can ask for access charges only if the grant has ended and running cost support ended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overheads eligibility and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Some organisations are eligible to request overheads on Wellcome grants; if requesting upload a letter from your Finance Director explaining calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If organisation has externally audited/verified methodology include confirmation of validated overhead rate, where documented, verifying organisation and last review. If not externally verified include breakdown of costs requested and confirmation it is a true representation. If UK university requesting overheads on subcontracted costs confirm university will not include these in its annual Charity Research Support Fund return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel and subsistence costs and environmental requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Request travel and subsistence costs in line with Wellcome's environmental sustainability funding policy; include conference attendance and other essential travel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conference attendance caps: up to £2,000/year for lead applicant and £1,000/year for research/technical staff unless strongly justified. For other travel provide detailed breakdown, host organisation, need, duration and mode of transport. Calculate emissions mitigation costs for all travel on the grant and state tonnes mitigated and cost to purchase accredited carbon credits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overseas allowances and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: If requesting overseas allowances select types (e.g., travel, baggage, insurance, visas, housing security, accommodation, education, annual leave travel, language lessons) and provide justification and costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe and justify each allowance and cost requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fieldwork expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: If requesting fieldwork expenses provide description, cost requested and justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include detailed justification of fieldwork needs and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical research costs
rubrics_metrics.description: If requesting clinical research costs provide description, cost requested and justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clinical research-specific justification and breakdown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public engagement and patient involvement costs
rubrics_metrics.description: If requesting costs for public engagement and patient involvement provide description, cost requested and justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how engagement activities support the research and why costs are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a detailed breakdown and justification of any other costs not covered by other categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter costs that do not fall under any other category and justify them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full economic costing (FEC) for UK organisations
rubrics_metrics.description: If your organisation is based in the UK indicate whether you are calculating the full economic cost of the proposal and state the total FEC in sterling including inflation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include inflation at the percentage rate used by your administering organisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: You may suggest reviewers particularly suitable to comment on your application or those you consider should not be approached (provide brief factual reason).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information provided here will not appear in the PDF of the application but will be visible to other participants involved in the application. Maximum 300 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding opportunity source reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Where did you find out about this funding opportunity? (select from list or specify)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is used for Wellcome reporting (options include professional organisation, conference, research office, colleague, Wellcome communications, LinkedIn, ResearchGate, social media, other).
